Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

options.A: Free goods are offered for sale at a loss-making price.
options.B: Merit goods generate more consumer surplus than producer surplus.

questions.questionText: Why does an individual’s demand curve generally slope downwards to the right?

options.A: The additional satisfaction an individual gets from consuming most goods decreases as consumption increases.
options.B: The additional satisfaction an individual gets from consumption decreases as income rises.
options.C: The individual has finite income which is used to attempt to satisfy many wants.
options.D: For most goods the price charged by producers falls as the quantity purchased increases.

questions.questionText: The soap industry consists of several firms. Firm X produces a small percentage of total output. What is likely to cause the supply curve for firm X to shift to the right while the market supply curve shifts to the left?

options.A: Firm X has improved technology while other firms have higher input costs.
options.B: Firm X has to pay a large fine for polluting a river while other firms have a tax reduction.
options.C: Firm X is involved in a strike while other firms enter the industry.
options.D: Firm X’s rent and interest charges increase while other firms receive a government subsidy.
